title: "The agent context & collaboration system"
subtitle: "How Flux makes an AI agent a real collaborator on your projects"
toc: true
number-sections: true
---

Flux is built so that an AI agent is a **first-class user** — everything the app can do, an agent can do through files and typed verbs. The context & collaboration system builds the layer above that: a **standing collaborator** (the *principal*) that knows who you are, knows each project's goals and history, takes your feedback without you leaving the app, and dispatches focused *worker* agents to do the heavy lifting.

The design has one organizing principle: **the files are the memory.** Everything the system knows — about you, about a project, about what has been tried and decided — lives in two plain-text `Context` folders. Any agent CLI that can read files (Claude Code, Codex, a future local model) can be the principal or a worker; swapping vendors is editing one config file, and nothing about your projects changes.

# The model

You talk to **one principal agent** per project — think of it as your senior postdoc. It reads your identity and standing rules, the project's mission, and its own running notebook at the start of every session, so it opens with a standup instead of asking you to re-explain anything. It handles judgment, conversation, and light edits itself, and **dispatches workers** — one-task agents launched with a complete written brief — for substantial analysis or coding. You review everything inside the Flux app and send feedback with a hotkey; the principal drains the queue and closes each item where you can see it.

Continuity comes from **rehydration, not process longevity**: the principal writes its memory down as it works, so a fresh session (tomorrow, or on a different model) picks up exactly where the last one stopped.

# Where everything lives

## Machine level — `<FluxConfig>/Context/`

Run `flux config` to print the resolved paths on your machine.

| Path | What it is | Who writes it |
|-----------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `Context/UserContext/WHO-AM-I.md` | Who you are: background, interests, strengths, taste. Every agent reads it at session start — the more it knows, the less you repeat yourself. | **You** |
| `Context/UserContext/RULES.md` | Your standing rules for *all* Flux work (figure conventions, writing style, statistics habits). Add sibling files or images freely — agents read everything in the folder. | **You** (agents may propose edits) |
| `Context/FluxContext/` | Stock documentation shipped with Flux and re-synced on every update — **the single canonical home of all agent-facing Flux knowledge.** Role docs: `README.md` (the map of this whole scheme), `PRINCIPAL.md` (the principal's role & doctrine), `WORKERS.md` (dispatched workers), `AGENTS-CONFIG.md` (the roster format). Working references: `FLUX-CLI.md`, `WORKFLOW.md` (the session playbook), `CLI-REFERENCE.md` (every verb), `PLOTS-AND-STYLE.md`, `PROJECT-AND-FIGURES.md`, `MANUSCRIPT-AND-REVIEW.md`, `SLIDES.md`, `PROJECT-GUIDE.md`, `TEMPLATES.md`. Machine-specific CLI/MCP invocations are baked in at sync time. | **Flux** — never edit these |
| `<FluxConfig>/agents.json` | The **agent roster**: which CLI is your principal, which are dispatchable workers (see @sec-roster). | **You** |

If you used Flux before this system existed, your old `Guidelines/` folder was migrated into `UserContext/` automatically on first run (your `base_rules.md` became `RULES.md`; every other file moved intact).

## Project level — `<project>/Context/`

Created for new projects and **healed into existing projects the first time you open them** (additive only — nothing of yours is touched). Also available on demand: `flux context-init`.

| Path | What it is | Who writes it |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `Context/Project/MISSION.qmd` | The project charter: question, data, prior work, deliverable, scope. The principal drafts it by *interviewing you* at project start and consults it whenever it needs to know "what are we driving toward?" | Co-owned — **you have final say** |
| `Context/NOTEBOOK.md` | The principal's full memory of the project: current state, decisions *and why*, what's been tried (including dead ends), open questions, plus an append-only session log. This is what makes the agent coherent across sessions. | **The agent** — you read it and leave comments |
| `Context/RULES.md` | Standing rules for *this* project only. When your feedback expresses a preference rather than a one-off fix, the principal promotes it here — so session ten needs less correcting than session one. | Co-owned |
| `Context/Transcripts/` | Timestamped transcripts of principal sessions run in the app's Agent drawer, captured by Flux itself from the terminal buffer. An archive — searched when needed, never required reading. | **Flux** (append-only) |
| `Context/Dispatches/` | One folder per worker dispatch: `brief.md` (the exact instructions the principal wrote), `log.txt` (full output), `result.md` (outcome). The audit trail of your principal's delegation — worth spot-checking. | **The principal** |

The three Context documents are **first-class Flux Paper documents**: they appear in a separate "Context" group of the document picker, open in the editor like any manuscript, and **review comments work on them** — you can annotate your agent's mission or its memory in the margin, and it treats those threads as corrections to address first.

`AGENTS.md` at the project root is now just a stub that routes any agent to the two Context folders (the old baked-in verb guide moved to `FluxContext/PROJECT-GUIDE.md`, where it updates with the app instead of going stale per-project).

## Operational files — `.meta/`

These are machinery, not memory — you normally never touch them.

| Path | What it is |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `.meta/feedback.ndjson` | The **feedback ledger**: your context-stamped notes, resolves, and send events. Event-sourced and append-only. |
| `.meta/journal.ndjson` | The provenance journal — every write, who made it, when. |
| `.meta/agent/status.json` | The attend watcher's heartbeat (`idle` / `working` / `done`). |
| `.meta/agent/passes/` | Logs of non-interactive review passes. |
| `manuscript/comments.json` | Review-comment threads for the main document (`<base>.comments.json` beside other documents, including Context docs). |

# The workflow

## One-time setup (per machine)

1.  Fill out `Context/UserContext/WHO-AM-I.md` — the seeded file says what to include.
2.  Skim `Context/UserContext/RULES.md` (your migrated conventions) and adjust.
3.  Optionally edit `agents.json` if you don't want the defaults (@sec-roster).

## Starting a project

Open (or scaffold) a project and press **Ctrl+Shift+J** — the Agent drawer opens with your principal booted on this project. On a fresh project the mission is still the template, so the principal **interviews you**: what's the question, where's the data, what's been done, what's the deliverable. It drafts `MISSION.qmd` from your answers; you read it in Flux Paper, edit or comment, and it revises until the charter reads true. That conversation is the last time you explain the project to anyone.

## A working session

Open the drawer (the session persists across mode switches; the conversation survives closing and reopening the drawer). The principal boots by reading UserContext → its doctrine → the mission → the notebook → the journal tail → open feedback, then gives a **standup**: what happened since last time, what's open, what it proposes first.

Talk at whatever level you want to think at. Light work it does directly; for anything substantial it writes a brief and runs `flux dispatch <role> --brief-file …` — the worker executes in the background, everything recorded under `Context/Dispatches/`. The principal reviews the result against the mission (rendering and *looking at* figures) before showing you. As it works, it keeps `NOTEBOOK.md` current — which you can watch live, since the app reloads Context docs like any external edit.

## The review loop

You review entirely inside the app:

-   **Comments** on any document (including Context docs) — threaded, anchored to exact text.
-   **Ctrl+Shift+M** anywhere — "Note to agent." Type one line; the note is **stamped with what you're looking at**: the active figure, selected elements, a drilled-in plot part, the document + selected text, or the slide + beat. "Make this bigger" arrives with *this* machine-resolved. The popover previews the stamp before you save.
-   **Send** (button in the popover, or the palette) — marks the review-pass boundary: everything open is now the agent's work order.

The principal drains both queues (`flux comments`, `flux feedback`), addresses each item, and resolves it with a note — you watch threads close and toasts appear live. When it isn't sure, it opens a comment thread *asking you* (`flux add-comment`) instead of guessing; answer in the margin whenever you like.

## While you're away

Leave `flux attend` running in a terminal. It watches the ledger; when you hit **Send**, it wakes one non-interactive principal pass (the `principalPass` roster entry) that drains the queue, resolves items, and updates the notebook — serialized, logged under `.meta/agent/passes/`, and idempotent across restarts. Only *new* sends trigger.

# The app surfaces

| Surface | Shortcut | What it does |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Command palette | **Ctrl+K** | Global commands everywhere (in Paper it opens Paper's full palette, which includes these): Open mission / notebook / project rules, open global rules / WHO-AM-I, toggle the drawer, Note to agent, Ask agent about this. |
| Agent drawer | **Ctrl+Shift+J** | Your principal in a real terminal, docked below the canvas in every mode. Transcripts are captured automatically. |
| Note to agent | **Ctrl+Shift+M** | The context-stamped feedback capture (+ the Send button). |
| Document picker | — | Context docs in their own group in the Paper sidebar. |

"Ask agent about this" opens the drawer and prefills (never auto-submits) a line describing your current selection.

# The command line

Everything above is also a verb — same behavior for any agent or script, and every verb is an MCP tool where that makes sense:

``` bash
flux config                # machine paths (Context, agents.json) + build info
flux context-init          # heal Context/ into a pre-existing project
flux feedback [--all]      # the ledger: open notes with their context stamps
flux resolve-feedback <id|text> --note "what I did"
flux send                  # mark a review-pass boundary
flux comments / resolve-comment / add-comment   # the comment loop (both directions)
flux agents                # show the roster
flux agent [--print]       # launch YOUR principal on this project, interactively
flux dispatch <role> --brief-file brief.md --name "new-dataset"
flux attend [--interval ms] [--echo]            # the send-wakes-a-pass watcher
```

# The agent roster — `agents.json` {#sec-roster}

`<FluxConfig>/agents.json` names the actual CLIs. The full format reference is `FluxContext/AGENTS-CONFIG.md`; the shape:

``` json
{
  "principal":     { "command": ["claude", "--mcp-config", "{mcpJson}",
                                 "--allowedTools", "mcp__flux", "{prompt}"] },
  "principalPass": { "command": ["claude", "-p", "{prompt}",
                                 "--permission-mode", "acceptEdits"] },
  "workers": {
    "analysis": { "command": ["claude", "-p", "{prompt}", "--permission-mode", "acceptEdits"] },
    "engineer": { "command": ["codex", "exec", "--full-auto", "{prompt}"] }
  }
}
```

Placeholders resolved at launch: `{prompt}` (the boot prompt or brief), `{briefPath}`, `{project}`, and `{mcpJson}` (the flux MCP server spec, so the principal gets typed Flux tools and inline figure PNGs). Each entry may set `cwd` (`"project"`, `"parent"`, or an absolute path — default is the parent directory when it looks like an analysis workspace, else the project) and extra `env`. `FLUX_PROJECT` and `FLUX_CLIENT` are always set for the child.

**This file is the whole vendor coupling.** The principal is a role defined by what it reads (the Context folders) and how it's launched (this roster) — change the command array and your collaborator gets a new brain with the same memory.

# Where the "skill" fits

Agent-CLI *skills* (the `~/.claude/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/` conventions) exist so a **bare, self-started session** can discover Flux unprompted. Since the principal and workers are launched *by* Flux with explicit pointers into FluxContext, they don't use the skill mechanism at all. What remains in the vendor skill directories is a deliberate **stub**: a few lines that trigger on Flux-related requests and route the agent to `<FluxConfig>/Context/` — it carries no knowledge of its own, so it never goes stale. All real content lives in FluxContext and updates with the app.

# Design properties worth knowing

-   **Agent-agnostic by construction.** Context is plain files; feedback and dispatch are files + spawned CLIs; transcripts are captured by the terminal host, not the agent. Nothing depends on any vendor's session store.
-   **Crash-safe.** The ledger is append-only (concurrent app + agent writers can't corrupt it); attend state survives restarts; a dead pass leaves notes open.
-   **Auditable.** Briefs, worker logs, transcripts, the journal, and the notebook give you a complete record of what your agents did and why.
-   **Self-improving.** The promotion discipline (feedback → RULES) and the notebook discipline (decisions written down as they're made) are stated in the stock `PRINCIPAL.md` doctrine — corrections compound instead of repeating.

# Troubleshooting

-   **Drawer says "unavailable"** — you're in the browser dev shell; the drawer needs the desktop app's PTY. Use `flux agent` in an external terminal instead.
-   **Drawer errors on launch** — the roster command isn't installed or the JSON is invalid; `flux agents` shows what resolved (a corrupt file falls back to defaults with a warning).
-   **A verb reports `deferred: … is locked`** — you're mid-edit in the app; the agent retries in a moment. This is the coexistence model working, not a bug.
-   **An old project has no Context docs** — open it once in the app, or run `flux context-init`.
